title: Memory retrieval, not logic, underlies almost all of human thinking

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Memory retrieval, not logic, underlies almost all of human thinking

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Retrieval from memory on the basis of similarity underlies almost every major aspect of human thinking, including generalization, analogy and intuition, and logical reasoning is not fundamental but is itself carried out by retrieving learned patterns of argument from memory.

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Ch. 10: Processes of Perception and Analysis

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: My strong suspicion is that the use of memory is what in fact underlies almost every major aspect of human thinking.

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci A New Kind of Science claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Stephen Wolfram, A New Kind of Science (Champaign, IL: Wolfram Media, 2002), Chapter 10, “Processes of Perception and Analysis”; section “Human Thinking” (from p. 620), p. 627. Scope: human cognition

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on wolfram2002-ch10-20: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.45

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Existing task data can assess memory involvement in selected forms of reasoning. They cannot establish that retrieval underlies almost every major aspect of thought or that logic is never a distinct computational mechanism.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Across reasoning, analogy, generalization, and intuition tasks, test whether trial-level behavior and neural activity are predicted by retrieval of learned episodes after controlling for explicit rule use and working memory. Selective disruption or absence of retrieval signatures would challenge restricted versions.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Retrieval and rule application are not mutually exclusive.

Neural correlates do not establish causal primacy.

The claim quantifies over almost all thinking.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
analysis feasibility: 0.4
data adequacy: 0.35
operationalizability: 0.38
discriminating power: 0.3
data existence: 0.72

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Cognitive datasets can address particular contrasts, such as analogy versus application of a stated rule. The claim says memory retrieval underlies almost all thinking and that logic itself is retrieved argument patterns. Those public resources cover fragments of that list, and most outcomes can be described in either the memory language or the rule language.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Across tasks that operationalize generalization, analogy, intuition, and deduction, test whether performance is predicted by similarity to stored instances rather than by application of content-free rules. A consistent memory-similarity account would support the claim; a dissociation in which logical performance tracks rule use and not retrieval would limit it.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Almost any reasoning trace can be redescribed as retrieval of a learned pattern.

'Almost every major aspect of human thinking' has no fixed task list.
